newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank says also to bring mark repos to Germany. [CORRECTED 16:17 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank says also to bring mark repos to Germany. [CORRECTED 16:17 GMT]

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG said on Wednesday it planned to bring its securities repurchase business in marks back to Frankfurt from London, effective February 1.

A spokesman for the bank, the third largest German commercial bank, confirmed the plans in response to a Reuters query and said the move was a response to the Bundesbank's decision in December to exempt some repo business from minimum reserve requirmements.
Earlier, Deutsche Bank AG management board member Rolf Breuer said the bank had firm plans to do the same.

As part of an effort to boost the attractiveness of Frankfurt as a financial centre, the Bundesbank in December freed up repos with maturities of up to one year from minimum reserve requirements -- which require banks to hold non-interest-bearing deposits with the central bank.

German banks had long lobbied to have the requirements lifted, since they argue they put them at a competitive disadvantage. Many had switched their main money market activities out of Germany to avoid the system.
However the Bundesbank also said it still viewed minimum reserves in general as an important monetary instrument and would continue to push for their use by the future European Central Bank.
Separately, Dresdner Bank AG, the second largest German bank, said its repo business had always stayed in Frankfurt, apart from business handled by its investment banking unit Kleinwort Benson.
